question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the maximum number of children less than 1 year old per caregiver?
quote: The minimum ratio of caregiver staff-to-children present at all times shall be as follows: Age of Children Number of Children to Caregiver Staff Less than 1 year 5
notes: Ratio must be met at all times, including opening/closing, field trips and swimming (Rule 1.8.2(2)). Maximum infant (birth through 12 months) group size is 10 (Rule 1.8.3).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the maximum number of 3-year-old children per caregiver?
quote: The minimum ratio of caregiver staff-to-children present at all times shall be as follows: Age of Children Number of Children to Caregiver Staff Less than 1 year 5 1 year 9 2 years 12 3 years 14
notes: Maximum group size for 3-year-olds is 28 (Rule 1.8.3). In mixed-age groups the youngest child's age sets the ratio (Rule 1.8.2(3)).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the maximum number of 4-year-old children per caregiver?
quote: The minimum ratio of caregiver staff-to-children present at all times shall be as follows: Age of Children Number of Children to Caregiver Staff Less than 1 year 5 1 year 9 2 years 12 3 years 14 4 years 16
notes: Maximum group size for 4-year-olds is 32 (Rule 1.8.3).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the maximum number of children aged 10 through 12 years per caregiver?
quote: The minimum ratio of caregiver staff-to-children present at all times shall be as follows: Age of Children Number of Children to Caregiver Staff ... 5 through 9 years 20 10 through 12 years 25
notes: 10 through 12 years is the oldest band (1:25, group of 50). Children 5 through 9 years are 1:20 (group of 40). Preschool children may not be grouped with school-age children (Rule 1.8.2(3)).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the maximum group size for a group of 4-year-old children?
quote: When children are placed in groups, the maximum group size shall be determined by the following chart. ... 4 years 32 children
notes: The same chart requires at least 2 caregivers for such a group. Group sizes need not be met during normal arrival/departure periods or special events, but ratios still apply (Rule 1.8.2(6)).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the minimum age for a caregiver?
quote: Caregivers shall be at least 18 years of age
notes: Caregiver assistants may be 16 (Rule 1.5.5) but must work under direct on-site supervision and may not be the sole caregiver responsible for a group.

question: Under Mississippi's child care director qualifications for a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, a director may qualify with a current Child Development Associate (CDA) credential plus paid caregiving experience in a licensed child care facility. How many years of that paid experience are required?
quote: Two years paid experience as a caregiver in a licensed child care facility, and either (1) a current Child Development Associate (CDA) credential
notes: One of five alternative routes. The director must also be at least 21. Other routes include a bachelor's degree in early childhood education or a related field, or an associate degree in child development technology.

question: How many contact hours of staff development must each caregiver, director and director designee at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi complete annually?
quote: All child care staff, directors, director designees, and caregivers shall be required to complete 15 contact hours of staff development, accrued during the licensure year, annually.
notes: No more than five hours of in-service training provided by the facility itself may count toward the 15 (Rule 1.5.8(4)).

question: What is the minimum usable indoor space per child used to set the licensed capacity of a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi?
quote: Every license shall set forth the licensed facility's maximum licensed capacity, which shall be based upon a minimum of thirty-five (35) square feet of usable indoor space per child.
notes: Infant rooms used for both play and sleep need 40 sq ft per child and toddler play-and-sleep rooms 45 (Rule 1.11.2(2),(5)). School-age-only programs need 25 (Rule 1.22.3). Kitchens, bathrooms, offices, hallways etc. are excluded.

question: What is the minimum outdoor playground area required for each child using the playground at any one time at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi?
quote: The outdoor playground area shall comprise a minimum of 75 square feet for each child using the outdoor playground area at any one time.
notes: Per child on the playground at one time. The total playground must also hold at least 33 percent of licensed capacity at one time (Rule 1.11.9(2)).

question: What is the maximum hot water temperature allowed at hand washing lavatories in a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi?
quote: All hand washing lavatories shall have both hot and cold running water. Hot water temperature shall not exceed 120 degrees Fahrenheit.

question: What document regarding medication must each child's individual file at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi contain?
answer: A signed written authorization to administer medication
quote: Authorizations ... Signed written authorization to obtain emergency medical treatment and to administer medication.
notes: The same signed authorization also covers obtaining emergency medical treatment. The rule does not say who signs it, but the file holds parental instructions and authorizations. A record of each dose (date, time, signature of dispensing employee) is also required (Rule 1.6.3(8)).

question: How often must a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi conduct fire drills?
quote: Emergency Drills: Child care providers shall: ... Conduct monthly fire and tornado drills
notes: Fire and tornado drills are monthly; all other disaster drills at least once every six months. Drill records must be kept on-site for the previous 12 months.

question: How long after a child stops attending must a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi keep that child's records?
quote: A child's records shall be retained for a period of one year after the child is no longer in attendance at the facility.
notes: All other records are kept at least three years unless otherwise specified (Rule 1.6.2(1)); medication records may be destroyed 90 days after the medication is given (Rule 1.6.3(8)).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, in what position must an infant be placed for sleeping, absent written physician orders to the contrary?
quote: An infant shall be placed on his/her back for sleeping unless written physician orders to the contrary are in the child's record.
notes: Only a written physician order in the child's record allows another position; a parent request is not enough.

question: When a serious occurrence happens at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, such as an injury requiring significant medical attention, when must the facility notify the child's parent and the licensing agency?
answer: Immediately (verbally or in writing); verbal notice must be followed by written confirmation within two days
quote: shall document any serious occurrences involving a child in the child's record and immediately notify the child's parent and the licensing agency either verbally or in writing, such as email.
notes: Verbal notifications must be followed by written confirmation sent within two days of the occurrence. If the parent or agency cannot be reached immediately, this must be noted in the child's record.

question: By when must a child enrolling in a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi have a Certificate of Immunization Compliance (Form 121) or a Certificate of Medical/Religious Exemption (Form 122)?
quote: The notebook shall contain separate current alphabetical rosters of both staff and children. All children ... must have one of the following forms before enrollment in a licensed child care facility: Certificate of Immunization Compliance (Form 121) or Certificate of Medical/Religious Exemption (Form 122)
notes: Children enrolled in a Summer Day Camp or School Age Program are not required to have Form 121 in their record (Rule 1.22.13).

question: During all hours of operation at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, including arrival and departure, how many staff members holding valid infant, child and adult First Aid and CPR certification must be present at minimum?
quote: First Aid and CPR Certification: During all hours of operation, including arrival and departure, child care providers shall have at least one staff member present that: a. Holds a valid infant, child, and adult First Aid and CPR certification.
notes: Rule 1.8.1(4) adds that the certified employee must be present at any location where children are present. Initial and renewal certification must be in-person, hands-on (no online-only courses).

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the minimum distance required between cribs in a room where infants both play and sleep?
quote: Rooms in which infants both play and sleep shall have a minimum of 40 square feet of usable space per child. There shall be at least 24” between each crib.
notes: 36 inches is recommended; cribs with solid ends may be placed end-to-end. Rule 1.10.9(6) also says cribs, cots and mats must be at least 24 inches apart or separated by a solid barrier.

question: How often may a license for a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi be renewed?
quote: The licensing agency shall issue licenses that may be renewed annually.
notes: The renewal application must be filed at least 30 days before the license expires; later online filing incurs a $25 late fee. A license not renewed before expiration lapses.

question: During rest periods at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, for children two years of age and older, what percentage of the required staff must be in the same room directly supervising the children, provided the full required ratio is maintained on the premises?
quote: With the exception of children under two years of age, children may be under the direct supervision (staff in the same room) of 50 percent of the staff required by this section during rest period times, provided the required staffto-child ratio is maintained on the premises.
notes: Does not apply to children under two: full ratio in the room for them.

question: May a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi group preschool children with school-age children in a single area during normal classroom and playground activities?
quote: In mixed age groups, the age of the youngest child in the group determines the staff-to-child ratio. Preschool children shall not be grouped with school age children in any single area during normal classroom and playground or water activities.
notes: Other mixed-age groups are allowed, using the ratio for the youngest child.

question: Of the 15 annual contact hours of staff development required at a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, how many hours of in-service training provided by the facility itself may count toward the total?
quote: No more than five contact hours of approved in-service training provided by the child care facility may be counted toward the total number of hours
notes: A facility may provide more in-service training, but only five hours count toward the 15.

question: If a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi notifies the licensing agency of a serious occurrence verbally, within how many days must written confirmation be sent?
quote: All verbal notifications must be followed by written confirmation, sent within two days of the occurrence.
notes: The first notice must be immediate (verbal or written); the two days count from the occurrence, not from the verbal call.

question: In a licensed child care facility (child care center) in Mississippi, what is the minimum usable space per child in a room where infants both play and sleep?
quote: Rooms in which infants both play and sleep shall have a minimum of 40 square feet of usable space per child.
notes: Exception to the general 35 sq ft standard. Infant play-only rooms need 15, infant sleep-only rooms 25, toddler play-and-sleep rooms 45 (Rule 1.11.2(3)-(5)).
